chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Umar ibn Yazid, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Say in the final prostration of the voluntary prayers of Maghrib on the night of Friday, while you are prostrating, seven times: "O God, I ask You by Your Noble Face and Your Great Name to send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and to forgive me my great sin."'

The Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: 'When the twilight fades, he should give the call to prayer for the final Isha prayer, up to the point of saying... and then lie down on his bed. The explanation of all of that has already passed.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite during the voluntary Maghrib prayer on Friday night?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Shia emphasis on specific devotional acts during the 'Night of Friday' (Laylat al-Jumu'ah), prescribing a unique supplication in the final prostration of voluntary Maghrib prayers. The invocation leverages the metaphysical power of God's 'Noble Face' and 'Great Name' to secure forgiveness, reflecting the tradition's focus on precise ritual timing and the spiritual merit of Friday nights. The reference to the final Isha prayer underscores the continuity of these practices within the broader framework of nightly worship detailed in the chapter.
